author: Vetsrx
quote:
GTA 6: Beautiful Graphics, but where did the fun go?
After waiting 13 years for GTA 6, I genuinely wish I could say it was worth it. Unfortunately, if I could go back and make the decision again, I probably wouldn't buy it. I'm considering requesting a refund.

I'll start with the positives. The graphics are phenomenal. Rockstar clearly put an incredible amount of effort into making the world look realistic. But there's a massive problem: 30 FPS. Coming from games that run at 60 FPS or higher, the difference is immediately noticeable. Beautiful graphics don't make up for gameplay that feels sluggish.

But my biggest disappointment isn't the frame rate. It's the lack of freedom.

Grand Theft Auto has always been about player choice. GTA 5 gave us Michael, Franklin, and Trevor, three very different characters with different personalities and motivations. Even the ending allowed us to make a significant decision about their futures.

GTA 6 felt like the opposite. Instead of having the freedom to make meaningful decisions, I felt like I was following an arrow down a predetermined path. The storyline felt predictable, the endings were cliché, and I struggled to connect with the characters.

And don't even get me started on the relationship management.

I didn't wait 13 years to play a simulator where I'm fixing a roof, painting walls, repairing stairs, and trying to keep my girlfriend happy so she doesn't leave me. I already have responsibilities in real life. I play video games to escape them.

It genuinely felt like I was playing a relationship simulator with occasional criminal activities thrown in.

The combat and driving didn't help either.

I'm not a fan of the free-aim gunplay. Vehicles felt clunky, aircraft felt clunky, and the overall gameplay never gave me that satisfying feeling I expected from a new GTA.

Then there's the professionalism system. Why am I being punished for defending myself against people actively trying to kill me?

Someone pulls a gun, starts shooting at me, and I'm supposed to worry about how professionally I handle the situation?

What am I supposed to do? Shoot the gun out of his hand, tip my cowboy hat, and say, "Not today, partner," before walking into the sunset?

This isn't a Clint Eastwood movie.

The restrictions on interacting with certain NPCs, including protesters, made the world feel even less free. I'm not saying everyone needs to play like a complete psychopath. I'm saying the player should have the choice, and the game world should respond accordingly.

That's what made GTA entertaining. You could be good, bad, reckless, responsible, or somewhere in between.

Instead, GTA 6 felt determined to tell me how I was supposed to play.

And where is the criminal empire fantasy?

You're pulling off heists, taking over criminal operations, and supposedly building something bigger. Yet somehow, you're still struggling financially.

What's the point of taking over an empire if you can't enjoy the rewards?

In GTA 5, making money meant buying cars, properties, upgrades, and enjoying the ridiculous lifestyle that came with being a successful criminal.

Here, it felt like I was working just to survive.

I'm already doing that in real life. Why would I want to spend my free time doing it again?

The lack of an autosave system in my experience was another frustrating issue. Having to constantly remember to save manually, with the possibility of losing progress, felt unnecessarily outdated.

Ultimately, GTA 6 looks incredible but feels incredibly disappointing.

The humor, the freedom, the memorable characters, the excitement of building wealth, and the ability to play the way you wanted were what made this franchise special to me.

I didn't feel that magic here.

When the credits rolled, I wasn't excited to jump back in. I wasn't thinking about replaying the story or exploring different outcomes.

I was thinking, "That's it?"

If GTA 6 Online follows the same direction, count me out. I'd rather return to GTA 5 and GTA Online, where I can actually enjoy the freedom that made me fall in love with this franchise.

Thirteen years of waiting for better graphics and less freedom isn't the evolution I wanted.

Rockstar made a beautiful world. I just wish they'd remembered to make it fun.
